Alarm, safety and warning systems are used to monitor a vast array of conditions in today's technical world.
Smoke detectors are used to detect and warn the occupants of a home or business of the possibility of fire.
Intrusion alarms are used in banks, businesses, homes, and even cars to alert of unauthorized access.
Exhaust gas, temperature, engine noise, and wheel speed are just a few of the items that are monitored by sensors and switches in today
s cars, to ensure their safe and proper operation.
Alarm, safety and warning systems are all around us. These systems are vital for the safe and successful operation of today's Navy.

text: BASIC ALARM, SAFETY AND WARNING SYSTEMS

Alarm, safety and warning systems are installed in Navy ships to alert personnel (watch standers) that a hazardous condition, equipment malfunction, or other abnormality requiring immediate action exists.
The use of these systems enables one operator (watch stander) to monitor equipment functions and the environmental conditions of remote equipment and spaces.
Alarm and warning systems provide an audible and, or visual indication when abnormal or dangerous conditions occur.
An alarm system consists of sensing devices, audible and visual indicating devices, and an alarm panel or switchboard.
Sensing devices initiate the alarm by sensing a deviation in the set parameter. In turn, this causes a switch or relay contact to close and energize the alarm-signaling device.

Audible and visual indicating devices are used to alert personnel that an alarm condition exists. Their type and location depend on the circuits they are used with, and also the environmental conditions within the spaces they are monitored at...
Alarm panels and switchboards are normally installed in spaces that are continuously manned both underway and inport.
Alarm panels are normally located within close proximity to the monitored condition, while switchboards are normally mounted in control spaces (i.e. DCC, CIC, Pilot House).
Alarm panels and switchboards are capable of monitoring a number of circuits, depending on the type and size of the panel or switchboard.
What is used to initiate alarms in the alarm, safety and warning system?
Sensing devices initiate the alarm by sensing a deviation in the set parameter. In turn, this causes a switch or relay contact to close and energize the alarm-signaling device.
There are three conditions of an alarm system:.............
Monitored parameter is within normal limits.
Monitored parameter is outside of normal limits.
Indicates a fault with the alarm circuit.
A normal condition exists when the system is functioning correctly. During this condition, a small continuous current flows in the circuit, which indicates that the circuit is in a normal condition.
An alarm condition exists when there is an increase in current flow in the circuit. This increase in current results when the sensing device senses a deviation in the set parameter.
A trouble (supervisory) condition exists when an open in the circuit stops the flow of current. Under this condition, an alarm condition cannot be detected.

IC/SM alarm switchboards are designed to give multiple steady and flashing displays, together with multiple audible signals in such a way that each "alarm condition" of the remote sensor is uniquely identified...
Controls and indicators on the alarm panel switchboard provide continuous monitoring of the condition/status of remote spaces and equipment.
Controls and indicators are divided into two sections known as the COMMON ALARM section and the LINE DISPLAY section.
The common alarm section contains the controls and indicators common to all monitored circuits on the panel.

Let's discuss the controls and indicators found on the common alarm section.
Ground detection indicator lights provide an indication, when a Positive ground or Negative ground condition exists in the wiring of the switchboard or the sensor circuit.
The POS indicator illuminates when the +DC bus becomes grounded.
The NEG indicator illuminates when the -DC bus becomes grounded.
The alarm lamp will illuminate when the visual-audible switch is in the VISUAL position and the equipment senses a supervisory or alarm signal.
The visual-audible alarm switch is a two-position switch that allows the operator a choice of either hearing audible alarm signals from the speaker, or seeing alarm signals on the alarm lamp...
The dimmer control permits dimming of all alarm module displays when they are on steady. Flashing displays are not effected by this control and will always illuminate at full brilliance.
All audible alarm signals are reproduced by the speaker....
The main power fuseholder contains the two main input power fuses for the equipment. The fuseholder will illuminate if either fuse is blown.
The extension signal fuses provide protection for the alarm and supervisory extension circuits. The fuseholders will illuminate when a fuse is blown and extension signal power is present.
What are the 3 basic circuit conditions for the alarm, safety and warning system?
There are three conditions of an alarm system:.............
Monitored parameter is within normal limits.
Monitored parameter is outside of normal limits.
Indicates a fault with the alarm circuit.
Now let's discuss the controls and indicators on the line display section.
There is one ALARM MODULE associated with each alarm (line) circuit. Each module contains a mode selector switch, two indicator lamps, and alarm detection circuitry.
The MODE SELECTOR SWITCH is a four position rotary switch.....
The STBY (standby) position is used to acknowledge an alarm condition.
The NORM (normal) position is the normal operating position. In this position the alarm module is indicating the current condition of the monitored circuit.
The CUTOUT position is used to secure power to the sensor for maintenance. (NEVER place in CUTOUT without proper authorization.)
The TEST position is used to simulate an alarm condition, testing the switchboard circuitry. (This position does not test the external wiring or sensors in the alarm circuit.)

The alarm module uses an UPPER and LOWER visual display in conjunction with the audible signal to indicate six possible status conditions of the alarm system, the seventh (power failure) is an overall switchboard condition affecting the entire alarm system...

The IC/SM alarm switchboard provides distinctive indications for three input conditions:ondition (sensor input circuit open).larm condition (fault at sense point); 3) supervisory condition (sensor input circuit open).

These indications are presented in the form of multiple steady and flashing lights together with multiple steady, pulsating, and wailing audible tones. Additionally, a power failure or a grounded circuit will be sensed...
While in a NORMAL condition the upper portion of the visual display indicator on each alarm module is steadily lighted and all other indicators are inactive.

While in an ALARM condition, the upper portion of the visual display on the module(s) sensing the alarm condition is lighted in a flashing manner. With the Visual/Audible switch in the audible position a siren wailing audible tone is produced...

With the Visual/Audible switch in the visual position the alarm lamp will illuminate in place of the audible tone. All other indicators are inactive (unless a supervisory or grounded circuit condition exists simultaneously)....

With the Visual/Audible switch in the visual position the alarm lamp will illuminate in place of the audible tone. All other indicators are inactive (unless a supervisory or grounded circuit condition exists simultaneously)...

A GROUNDED circuit condition indicates problems in the 6VDC buses. During this condition, one of the ground detection indicator lights will be illuminated. All other indicators are inactive (unless an alarm or supervisory condition exists simultaneously)...
A POWER FAILURE condition occurs when input power is interrupted. An internal battery supplies the necessary power to produce a pulsating audible tone. All other indicators are inactive..
Now let's cover the operation of the mode selector switch.
With the alarm module selector switch in the NORM position the panel is monitoring the alarm circuit (loop) for any abnormal condition. Note: This is the standard operating position.

The STBY position is used to acknowledge an alarm condition. By placing the alarm module selector switch to STBY position during an alarm condition, the audible alarm will be silenced and both upper and lower visual display windows will illuminated steady...

In this standby mode the alarmed line circuit is being monitored for a change in status. When the alarmed condition returns to normal, the upper visual display will extinguish and the lower visual display will illuminate in a flashing manner. Additionally a siren wailing audible tone will sound...

By returning the mode selector switch to the NORM position the audible alarm will silence and the lower visual display will extinguish. The upper visual display will illuminate steady returning the alarm panel to the normal mode of operation...

The alarm panel requires external sensing devices to monitor equipment functions or environmental conditions of remote equipment and spaces.
Some of the common alarm sensors used in the Navy today are:

The door mounted switch activates an alarm when a door is opened or closed, and is used for brig door alarms, secure communication space alarms, and any other space that may require an intrusion alarm.

Door mounted switches utilizes a roller armature assembly and a door strike plate to operate a set of internal micro-switches. When the door is opened or closed, the strike plate causes the roller armature to rise, operating the internal switches and closing the contacts...
An additional set of internal switches are utilized as an anti-tamper device for the door switch cover. If the cover is loosened or removed the internal switches activate a tamper alarm.
The liquid level float switch activates an alarm when a liquid reaches a predetermined level. The switch can be used as either a low, normal, or high-level alarm.

The float switch utilizes a doughnut-shaped, floatable magnetic core operating over an encapsulated reed switch. Some models use a reversible float to change the switch configuration from N.O. contacts to N.C. contacts...
When the liquid rises to the predetermined level, the float rises. The magnetic core of the float causes the encapsulated reed switch to close, activating the level alarm.

Liquid level float switches can be found in main engine room bilges, auxiliary machinery room bilges, steering gear rooms, tanks, voids, weapons magazines, and any other spaces that may have high volumes of water flowing through them...

Detroit switch is the common name for Navy pressure and temperature switches. They are used to monitor ships equipment. (i.e. ships service turbine generators, ships service diesel generators, ships main engines, refrigeration units, etc.)))

The pressure switch is used to monitor the pressure of lube oil, water, air, or any other pressurized medium related to the safe operation of ships equipment. Normal operating ranges are, 0-15 PSI, 15-50 PSI, and 50-100 PSI. Pressure switches can be either cut in low pressure or cut in high pressure.

The temperature switch is used to monitor lube oil temperature, water temperature, bearing temperature and many other equipment temperature parameters. There are two types of temperature switch either cut in low temperature or cut in high temperature...

Both pressure and temperature switches operate utilizing a bellows working against an adjustable spring to activate a single pole/ single throw (SPST) switch. The closing of the (SPST) switch in the Detroit switch activates the alarm...

The temperature switch utilizes an expanding liquid, sealed within a capillary to sense the temperature. As the temperature raises the liquid in the capillary expands, exerting pressure on the bellows...
The pressure switch utilizes the actual pressure of the sensed medium to apply pressure to the bellows.
The mercury thermostatic switch is used to detect the presence of fires or overheated conditions in important compartments or spaces.
Note: NEVER paint a mercury thermostatic switch.

Mercury switches are available in three temperature ranges and each space can have as many switches as needed for coverage. They can be identified by colored bands on the bottom of the protective shield surrounding the glass tube...
The mercury thermostatic switch operates like a thermometer, utilizing a column of mercury to short across a set of three electrical contacts, all within a sealed glass tube.
During a normal temperature condition the mercury is low in the glass tube shorting the two lowest contacts. Current flows through the switch supporting the supervisory function of the alarm system.

During a high temperature condition the column of mercury will rise reaching the top contact. Current now flows from the bottom contact through the mercury to the top contact activating the high temperature alarm...

If the glass tube breaks, the mercury will drain from the switch. The loss of mercury in the switch will open the bottom two contacts, preventing the flow of current in the circuit and activating the trouble (supervisory) alarm.

Water switches activate an alarm during operation of the magazine sprinkling system. The switch contains two button contacts. When the saltwater fills the switch casting it shorts the two contacts activating the alarm....
After each use the drain plug must be removed, water drained, and the plug replaced! Maintenance is required after each use due to saltwater corrosion of the internal switch parts.
The ionization detector activates an alarm in the presence of smoke or combustible gases. Charged electrons provide the current increase for the alarm
Relay switches are used in critical circuits to sense power failure. Power failure causes the relay contacts to close initiating the alarm.
You have completed the information on BASIC ALARM, SAFETY AND WARNING SYSTEMS.
1. The basic alarm system consists of a sensing device, an alarm panel or switchboard, and audible or visual indicating devices..
2. Sensing devices are used with alarm, safety, and warning systems to initiate alarms when there is a deviation in normal operation..
3. Audible and visual signals are used with the alarm, safety, and warning systems to alert personnel that an alarm condition exists..
4. The three alarm conditions are normal, alarm, and trouble.
Monitored parameter is within normal limits.
Monitored parameter is outside of normal limits.
Indicates a fault with the alarm circuit.
5. The IC/SM alarm panel/switchboard enables one watch stander to monitor remote equipment and spaces, by providing a distinct audible and visual indication of each alarm condition...
6. Door mounted switches are used to sense the opening and closing of secure spaces...
7. The liquid level float switch is used to monitor for low, normal, and high levels in tanks, voids, bilges, or any other spaces that may be at risk of flooding.
8. A pressure switch uses a bellows that works against an adjustable spring, to operate a set of contacts. The pressure of the monitored medium operates the bellows.

9. A temperature switch uses a bellows that works against an adjustable spring, to operate a set of contacts. The bellows motion is produced by a sealed-in liquid that expands with rising temperature...
10. Mercury thermostatic switches make use of the encapsulated mercury to short the contacts of the switch.
11. A water switch is used primarily in magazine sprinkling alarm systems, and utilizes the water in the system to short the contacts.
12. Ionization detectors are used to detect the presence of combustible gases and smoke.
13. Relay switches are used to sense a loss of power in critical circuits.
